investigation.rootCause: The eval probe for runtimeEnvironment=production-api called /api/generate/image/stream via apiSse (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1438) and received a 404 before any generation work could begin. The stream emitted generation_start then immediately generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the agent runtime session could not be opened because the harness endpoint was not found at the configured base URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api harness target; it is not evidence of a user-facing image generation outage, as the desktop-release sibling check passed successfully in the same run window.

The quota ceiling prevented the eval's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1339) from succeeding, so the probe exited before writing any required evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production-api runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to end users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

The eval probe's createAgent call is blocked before any runtime response evidence can be collected, causing all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be absent.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org agent quota of 100. At the time the observability eval ran, the eval's org had already reached that limit, so every POST /api/agents call returned HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because agent creation is the first step in the runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1372: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)), no agent was provisioned and no downstream evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was ever captured. This is an eval infrastructure failure caused by a resource-limit condition in the production swarm API for the eval's org; no user-traffic or production incident signals are present in the evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely: the eval's org account has accumulated 100 swarm agents (from prior eval runs or other activity) and the swarm backend is enforcing its hard quota, rejecting all new agent creation attempts with HTTP 409.
Less likely but possible: a prior eval run's cleanup step (withCleanup) failed to delete one or more agents, causing agents to accumulate across runs until the quota was reached.
Less likely: the quota limit was recently lowered on the swarm backend for the eval org, causing previously-passing runs to now hit the ceiling.
Least likely: a transient swarm-side misconfiguration is incorrectly reporting the quota as exceeded when it is not actually at 100 agents.

If the swarm API logs show the 409 was returned for a different reason (e.g., duplicate agent name collision rather than quota), the root cause would shift to a naming/idempotency issue in the eval runner.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on production-api — Agent Runtime Harness Unreachable
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (latencyMs=2042) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying a 404 status, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint targeted by the eval probe was unreachable or returned an incompatible response. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime environment (latencyMs=129886, imageUrlPresent=true, generation_completed frame present), isolating the failure strictly to the production-api harness configuration and not to the image generation feature itself.
investigations.rootCause: The eval probe for runtimeEnvironment=production-api called /api/generate/image/stream via apiSse (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1438) and received a 404 before any generation work could begin. The stream emitted generation_start then immediately generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the agent runtime session could not be opened because the harness endpoint was not found at the configured base URL (LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL). This is an eval infrastructure connectivity failure scoped to the production-api harness target; it is not evidence of a user-facing image generation outage, as the desktop-release sibling check passed successfully in the same run window.
proof: failed-check.evidence: generation_error frame carries code=SESSION_OPEN_FAILED and message='agent runtime endpoint not found (404): the harness is unreachable or running an incompatible version. Verify the harness deployment and the LOCAL_HARNESS_URL / SWARM_BASE_URL configuration.'

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=2042 — the check completed in ~2 seconds, far below the warningLatencyMs=180000 threshold, confirming the failure was an immediate connection rejection rather than a timeout or slow generation.

failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed = [generation_start, generation_error, message]; generation_completed is absent and imageUrlPresent=false, directly causing both contract assertion failures.

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes contains 'generation_completed' and imageUrlPresent equals true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 271–272); neither was satisfied.

sibling.image-generation-stream: the same check on runtimeEnvironment=desktop-release passed with imageUrlPresent=true and generation_completed present in frameTypes, proving the image generation capability itself is functional and the failure is environment-specific.

source.check-config.image-generation-stream: the production-api check is registered as required=false with statusImpact=informational, meaning this failure does not constitute a declared service outage.

source.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1438: the probe calls apiSse(args, '/api/generate/image/stream', ...) — the 404 was returned against this endpoint in the production-api harness context.
possibleCauses: The production-api harness (resolved via LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL) was not deployed, was down, or was pointing to a URL that does not host the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint at the time of the eval run.
The SWARM_BASE_URL or LOCAL_HARNESS_URL environment variable was misconfigured or missing for the production-api eval runner context, causing the probe to target a wrong or non-existent host.

The production-api harness was deployed at an incompatible version that removed or renamed the /api/generate/image/stream route, causing a 404 for that specific endpoint while the host itself was reachable.
The production-api harness deployment was in a transient restart or rollout state at 2026-06-17T00:05:15Z, making the endpoint temporarily unavailable.
